prerequisites: Mathematics: Vector calculus and operations with complex numbers; resolution of systems of linear equations and quadratic equations; trigonometry; differential and integral calculus (concepts of derivation and integration, derivative and integral of simple functions); knowledge and use of trigonometric, exponential, and logarithmic functions.
Electromagnetism: Especially Electromagnetic Induction (seen in "Physics" and "Fields and Waves" courses).
Circuit Theory: Deep and solid knowledge of Electrical Circuit Analysis, especially the behavior of circuits in sinusoidal steady state in both single-phase and three-phase systems.

Fundamentals of Electrical Machines: Knowledge and prior review of the fundamentals of electrical machines, which can be acquired through the "Electrical Machines I" course or through courses such as "Fundamentals of Electrical Technology", "Electrical Installations and Machines" or similar.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability for the calculation and design of electrical machines.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge derived from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.

That students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
That students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other analogous tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.

syllabus_topics: UD 2 - Extension of Asynchronous or Induction Machines
teaching_methods: Work with theoretical content, utilizing basic and complementary bibliography, allowing for a general and detailed vision of learning objectives. This activity will be complemented by visiting websites of main electrical machine manufacturers, whose technical content (catalogs, application sheets, technical articles, etc.) will help provide a practical and real vision of the machines studied.
Completion of practical activities consisting of evaluation tests, solved exercises, and previous years' exams, supported and supervised by tutors.
Autonomous study of theoretical and practical contents. Preparation and completion of face-to-face tests.
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 95% of the Presential Exam grade + 4% of the Continuous Assessment Tests (PEC) grade + 1% of the Laboratory Practices grade. To pass the course, it is essential to pass the Presential Exam and have completed and passed the Laboratory Practices in the same academic year. The Presential Exam consists of 10 multiple-choice questions and two problems; a minimum score of two out of ten points is required in each of these three parts to pass the exam. The PEC grade always serves to increase the grade obtained in the Presential Exam, provided the Presential Exam is passed. Laboratory practices are mandatory and passing them (APTO) is essential to pass the course.
